A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AuToMATo study. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendix A are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original clustering benchmark results in Tables 1–9 and Mapper experiments on concentric-circle and diabetes data in Figures 5–6.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark and Mapper experiments and reports additional Iris benchmark results.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same ToMATo-based procedure, bootstrap sampling, treatment of infinite-lifetime features, and prominence-threshold selection. The revised description of parameter freedom does not change the algorithm.

E1.justification: Appendix A.2 adds Iris-related benchmark coverage through other_iris_0 and other_iris5_0 in Tables 2–9. Existing benchmark cases and both Mapper datasets remain. The PDFs do not explain how the two Iris variants differ.

E2.justification: The benchmark comparisons retain DBSCAN, HDBSCAN, four hierarchical linkage methods, FINCH, and TTK. The Mapper comparisons retain DBSCAN and HDBSCAN. No comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: The stated protocol retains min-max scaling, Fowlkes-Mallows scoring, outlier masking, baseline defaults, and the distance-threshold sweep from 0.05 to 1.00 in increments of 0.05. The aggregation rules also remain unchanged; no protocol revision is documented alongside the updated scores.

E4.justification: The two Mapper case studies and their findings are retained in Section 5 and Figures 5–6. No ablation, sensitivity study, robustness test, or additional case study is introduced.

E5.justification: Figures 4 and 7–14 add shaded variability bands around AuToMATo's mean curves, whereas v1 shows unbanded curves. Both versions already report ten runs, fixed-seed information, and tabulated means and standard deviations. The bands are not precisely defined, and additional replication is not documented.

E6.justification: Tables 2–9 add Iris results and revise some existing scores. For example, TTK on fcps_atom_0 changes from 1.0000 to 0.8472, reversing its comparison with unchanged AuToMATo at 0.8694. Table 1 changes AuToMATo's average from 0.8620±0.0202 to 0.8554±0.0228 while retaining the overall ranking. These aggregates cover different benchmark sets and therefore do not establish a same-setting performance decline.

T1.justification: Section 2.4 corrects the FN counting definition from data points to pairs of data points. The Fowlkes-Mallows formula, persistence definitions, bootstrap derivation, and Appendix A.1 complexity analysis otherwise remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The title, abstract, and introduction withdraw the central claim that AuToMATo is parameter-free. v2 explicitly acknowledges parameters and presents the contribution as an algorithm with fixed defaults that avoids tuning. This substantially narrows the headline property claimed for the method, while retaining the performance and Mapper claims.

C2.justification: Section 2.4 adds a substantive rationale for rejecting intrinsic clustering metrics. Section 4.2 clarifies the existing exclusion of olympic by correctly attaching the single-connected-component explanation to that dataset. The parameter-dependence and outlier limitations in Section 6 are retained.

D1.justification: Implementation details, default parameters, seed and parallelization support, hardware information, and code/data access disclosures are retained. Removing the introductory repository footnote does not remove access information because the same repository remains identified in Section 3.2.

R1.justification: AuToMATo is repositioned from a parameter-free peer of FINCH and TTK to an algorithm whose fixed defaults are compared with parameter-free methods. Cited-work membership is unchanged; RVBV16 and RNBV16 refer to the same paper with revised bibliographic metadata.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, and introduction receive localized rewrites. The metric-selection rationale moves from Section 4.3 to Section 2.4 and is expanded, alongside small wording and contact-information edits. The overall section organization remains intact.

P2.justification: Figure 3 swaps the windows and olympic panels and explicitly labels their positions. Benchmark plots gain mean labels, shaded bands, and Iris entries; tables are reordered and repaginated, and Figure 4 moves to the next page. The existing figure/table inventory and basic display formats remain.

improvement.justification: v2 corrects the misleading parameter-free headline to match the defaults already disclosed in v1 and clarifies the evaluation rationale. Iris results and plotted variability provide modest additional coverage and transparency, although the bands are not precisely defined. The underlying method, theory, and main empirical conclusions remain stable.
